hero.title: Hadith Hotel
hero.supporting: Where Samarkand's heritage meets the warmth of Indonesian hospitality — a contemporary tribute to Imam Al Bukhari.

concept.title: A Landmark Tribute at the Spiritual Heart of Samarkand
concept.body1: Hadith Hotel is presented as a contemporary five-star hotel honouring the hadith scholar Imam Al-Bukhari — blending Silk Road grandeur with attentive Indonesian hospitality and Indonesian coffee culture.
concept.body2: Its signature narrative describes 114 rooms as reflecting the surahs of the Qur'an. Operating status, full room-category breakdown, and facility hours are to be confirmed with the client.

place.title: Within the Imam Al Bukhari Complex
place.body: Samarkand, Uzbekistan — set within the Imam Al Bukhari Complex, often described as the spiritual heart of Samarkand.
place.landmark: The courtyard features a Monument of Soekarno — framed as a shared Indonesia–Uzbekistan heritage gesture.

rooms.title: 114 Rooms
rooms.text: Total inventory of 114 rooms as stated in project materials. Documented examples include Standard Rooms (62 rooms, 35 m²) and Junior Suites (9 rooms, 71 m², 24-hour butler). A full published tier list is to be provided.

dining.title: Dining & 7OZ Espresso
dining.text: The Restaurant — signature dining (120 seats) with Uzbek, Indonesian, and Continental cuisine, stated as halal. The Bar & Lounge — Indonesian pastries and specialty coffees, including Kopi Luwak. Confirmed: 7OZ Espresso also operates at Hadith Hotel. Opening hours are to be confirmed.

wellness.title: Wellness & Recreation
wellness.text: Heated swimming pool with sauna; spa (Nusantara / Balinese); Turkish hammam; fitness centre; tennis and padel courts; kids playground. Facility hours are to be confirmed.

mice.title: Meetings & Events
mice.text: Convention / ballroom of 350 m², stated capacity up to 250 guests — suited to MICE and celebration gatherings.

services.title: Guest Services
services.text: Grand lobby; 24-hour multilingual concierge; Wall of Fame / gallery; boutique featuring Uzbek and Indonesian craftsmanship. Land area stated at approximately 62,000 m².

rating.title: Class
rating.text: Presented as a five-star (5★) hotel in source materials. Certifying authority is to be confirmed.

hero.supporting: A boutique halal address opposite Uzbekistan's flagship Islamic landmark — compact in scale, deliberate in position.

concept.title: Boutique Scale, Landmark Position
concept.body1: Mecca Boutique Hotel & Restaurant is a four-star boutique hotel with 30 rooms inspired by the 30 Juz of the Qur'an — designed for Asia halal travellers, regional business guests, and pilgrims.
concept.body2: All dining venues are stated as halal-certified. Operating status and opening date are to be confirmed with the client.

place.title: Opposite the Centre of Islamic Civilization
place.body: Tashkent, Uzbekistan — directly opposite the Tashkent Centre of Islamic Civilization, with boulevard frontage. Approximately 30 minutes to the airport and 20 minutes to the railway station, as stated in source materials.
place.landmark: Rooftop views look toward the Islamic Civilization Centre dome — anchoring the hotel's sense of place.

rooms.title: 30 Guest Rooms
rooms.text: Thirty uniform guest rooms (~18 m², queen), qibla-marked and provided with a prayer mat. Three floors plus rooftop; land area 3,000 m²; built-up area 3,038.7 m² as stated.

indonesiaResto.title: Indonesia Resto
indonesiaResto.text: Authentic Indonesian dining on the ground floor (497 m²), with Indonesian chefs. Named dishes in source materials include Rendang, Nasi Goreng, Sate, Soto, and Gado-Gado. Full menus and hours are to be provided.

europeResto.title: Europe Resto
europeResto.text: European cuisine on the second floor (452 m²) — including fresh pasta, risotto, wood-fired pizza, osso buco, and tiramisu as cited. Positioned as premium European dining. Menus and hours are to be provided.

rooftop.title: Rooftop Café — 7OZ
rooftop.text: A 600.7 m² terrace café — coffee, light meals, and shisha as listed in source materials — with views to the Islamic Civilization Centre dome. This rooftop café is 7OZ Espresso, EBI Resources' specialty-coffee brand (also at Hadith Hotel in Samarkand). How shisha sits alongside the hotel's stated halal dining certification is to be confirmed with the client.

services.title: Guest Services
services.text: Double-height lobby and reading lounge; prayer room; 24-hour concierge; multilingual front desk (Uzbek, Russian, English, Indonesian, Arabic). Event capability up to 500 guests (banquet/event capacity). No spa, gym, or pool is listed in sources.

rating.title: Class
rating.text: Presented as a four-star (4★) boutique hotel in source materials. Certifying authority is to be confirmed.

gus-irfan-visits-hotel-kampoeng-indonesi.title: Gus Irfan Visits Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia at the Imam Bukhari Complex, Samarkand
gus-irfan-visits-hotel-kampoeng-indonesi.excerpt: Indonesia’s Minister of Hajj and Umrah visited Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia during an official programme in Samarkand.
gus-irfan-visits-hotel-kampoeng-indonesi.alt: Official visit at Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia, Samarkand
body: Indonesia’s Minister of Hajj and Umrah, Mochamad Irfan Yusuf — known as Gus Irfan — visited Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia in the Imam Bukhari memorial complex, Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The visit took place during his official programme in Samarkand, after accepting an invitation from the Governor of Samarkand, Adiz Muzaffarovich Boboev. During the visit, Gus Irfan joined a midday meal of Indonesian dishes prepared at the hotel.

Gus Irfan welcomed Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia as part of EBI Resources’ investment from Indonesia in Uzbekistan. The Indonesian-concept hotel is regarded as a way to introduce Indonesian cuisine, culture, and identity in a place that draws travellers and pilgrims from many countries. The visit also offered a first-hand look at facilities that carry an Indonesian atmosphere within the Imam Bukhari complex.

In addition to Hotel Kampoeng Indonesia, Gus Irfan visited the Imam Bukhari memorial complex and paid respects at the shrine. He was accompanied by Indonesia’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Siti Ruhaini Dzuhayatin. The programme formed part of his working visit to Samarkand and of closer ties between Indonesia and Uzbekistan.

hadith-hotel-soft-opening-samarkand.title: Hadith Hotel Holds Soft Opening in Samarkand
hadith-hotel-soft-opening-samarkand.excerpt: Hadith Hotel marked its soft opening at the Imam Al Bukhari Complex on Saturday, 5 September 2026.
hadith-hotel-soft-opening-samarkand.alt: Hadith Hotel soft opening in Samarkand
body: EBI Resources held the soft opening of Hadith Hotel at the Imam Al Bukhari Complex, Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Saturday, 5 September 2026. The hotel is a further step for Indonesian hospitality in Central Asia, a region with strong potential in tourism, hospitality, and pilgrimage travel.

The soft opening was attended by figures from Indonesia and Uzbekistan, including Indonesia’s Minister of Hajj and Umrah, Mochamad Irfan Yusuf; Indonesia’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Prof. Dr. Siti Ruhaini Dzuhayatin; and Indonesia’s Ambassador to Kazakhstan, M. Fadjroel Rachman. Their presence reflected closer Indonesia–Uzbekistan relations and the scope for economic and investment cooperation in the region.

Management of EBI Resources underlined that Hadith Hotel offers international-standard accommodation while carrying Indonesian hospitality onto a global stage. The hotel includes 114 rooms and suites, Indonesian dining, an Uzbek cuisine lounge, an indoor pool, spa, sauna, Turkish hammam, tennis, and a padel court. It is intended to support Samarkand’s international tourism and to strengthen EBI Resources’ presence abroad.

hadith-hotel-near-imam-bukhari.title: Near the Imam Bukhari Shrine, Hadith Hotel Brings an Indonesian Touch to Samarkand
hadith-hotel-near-imam-bukhari.excerpt: Hadith Hotel opened beside the Imam Al Bukhari Complex, combining Uzbek setting with international comfort.
hadith-hotel-near-imam-bukhari.alt: Hadith Hotel at the Imam Al Bukhari Complex, Samarkand
body: Hadith Hotel held its soft opening at the Imam Al Bukhari Complex, Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Saturday, 5 September 2026. Less than a kilometre from the shrine of Imam Muhammad Al-Bukhari, the hotel — developed by EBI Resources — offers modern accommodation that brings together an Uzbek setting and international comfort.

Hadith Hotel has 114 rooms and suites, with occupancy for up to 250 guests. Five room types serve pilgrims, travellers, and VIP guests: 62 Standard Rooms, 23 Balcony Rooms, 18 Suites, 9 Junior Suites, and 2 President Suites. Its place within the Imam Al Bukhari precinct is well suited to visitors coming for pilgrimage and for Samarkand’s history and culture.

Beyond accommodation, Hadith Hotel offers Indonesian dining, an Uzbek cuisine lounge, an indoor pool, a fitness centre, spa, sauna, Turkish hammam, tennis, and a padel court. The hotel is intended to strengthen hospitality in Samarkand and to serve as a cultural bridge between Indonesia and Uzbekistan through travel and Nusantara hospitality.

ambassador-meets-ceo-hadith-opening.title: Indonesia’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan Meets the CEO of EBI Resources on Tourism Cooperation
ambassador-meets-ceo-hadith-opening.excerpt: In Jakarta on 31 August 2026, the ambassador and the CEO discussed investment in Uzbekistan and the inauguration of Hadith Hotel.
ambassador-meets-ceo-hadith-opening.alt: Meeting on tourism cooperation and the Hadith Hotel inauguration
body: Jakarta, 31 August 2026 — The CEO of EBI Resources received Indonesia’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan to discuss the next steps in the group’s investment in Uzbekistan. On that occasion the CEO invited the Ambassador to attend the inauguration of Hadith Hotel at the Imam Al Bukhari memorial complex in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The two sides also discussed the potential for EBI Resources to expand its investment in Uzbekistan, and the importance of more Indonesian travellers visiting Uzbekistan for general tourism and pilgrimage.

The Ambassador welcomed the idea of more visitors travelling between Indonesia and Uzbekistan, which is expected to be supported by a planned direct flight between Jakarta and Tashkent in the near term. She expressed the hope that EBI Resources’ investment in Uzbekistan, together with that planned route, would strengthen tourism cooperation between the two countries.

Both sides also hoped that closer investment and socio-cultural ties would be matched by closer government-to-government cooperation, including high-level visits, to further strengthen bilateral relations between Indonesia and Uzbekistan.
